levels.title: Scientific Computing, Research Tooling & Reproducibility
levels.scope: Establish the core computing and software environment required for scientific research in Computer Science, Data Science, and AI/ML: remote Linux cluster navigation, containerized environments, deterministic hardware seeding, experiment logging, and open-source scientific repository standards.
levels.prereqStated: None (introductory on-ramp for Bachelor's, Master's, and prospective graduate researchers)

modules.name: The Research Computing Stack: Linux, Remote Servers & GPU Monitoring

objectives.text: - Connect to institutional and laboratory GPU compute servers via SSH using public-key cryptography, custom config hosts, and SSH agent forwarding.
objectives.group: Remote Linux Compute Environments & Process Persistence

objectives.text: - Manage persistent long-running research jobs across network drops using terminal multiplexers (tmux, screen) with multi-window workflows.
objectives.group: Remote Linux Compute Environments & Process Persistence

objectives.text: - Monitor active server processes, memory consumption, and CPU core affinity using htop, ps, and process kill signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL).
objectives.group: Remote Linux Compute Environments & Process Persistence

modules.outcome: Navigate remote Linux research environments, manage persistent background experiments, and diagnose hardware compute bottlenecks.

modules.name: Reproducible Scientific Environments: Pixi, Conda, Docker & PyPI

objectives.text: - Understand the reproducibility crisis in AI/ML research caused by unpinned transitive dependencies, Python version drift, and conflicting CUDA libraries.
- Isolate scientific Python environments using modern package managers (Pixi, uv, Conda) with locked dependency trees and reproducible manifests.
- Install and compile C++/CUDA extensions from source within user environments without corrupting host system operating system libraries.
- Author multi-stage Dockerfiles optimized for deep learning research containing specific CUDA, cuDNN, and PyTorch/JAX runtime versions.
- Mount host scratch disks and dataset volumes into isolated containers with non-root user permissions and shared memory flags (--shm-size).
- Export locked environment manifests (environment.lock.yml, pyproject.toml) ensuring bitwise reproducible execution across disparate research clusters.

modules.mentalModel: A research environment must be an immutable, containerized artifact so that any researcher can reproduce exact numerical results five years later.
modules.tryIt: Build a reproducible Docker image pinning PyTorch and CUDA runtime dependencies, mounting an external dataset volume with non-root permissions.
modules.outcome: Eliminate dependency drift, resolve CUDA library mismatches, and package research experiments into containerized scientific artifacts.

modules.name: Version Control for Science: Git, Submodules & Open-Source Code Release

objectives.text: - Structure research codebases separating reusable library code, model definitions, baseline benchmarks, and exploratory experimental scripts.
- Use feature branches and semantic Git tags to mark paper submission checkpoints, rebuttal revisions, and camera-ready milestones.
- Manage external baseline codebases and upstream research libraries cleanly using Git submodules and subtree merges.
- Author comprehensive academic README files featuring installation commands, pretrained checkpoint links, and minimal reproduction snippets.
- Include open-source research licensing (Apache 2.0, BSD 3-Clause, CC-BY) and BibTeX citation blocks formatted for Google Scholar and ArXiv indexing.
- Prevent confidential dataset leakage and credential exposure by strictly configuring .gitignore for checkpoints, logs, raw data, and API keys.

modules.mentalModel: Git tags in research serve as immutable cryptographic stamps linking paper figures and tables directly to specific commit hashes.
modules.tryIt: Create a research template repository with a structured module layout, automated linter, .gitignore, and standardized BibTeX citation header.
modules.outcome: Structure academic research repositories to meet top-tier conference artifact evaluation and reproducibility standards.

modules.name: Experiment Tracking & Artifact Management: Weights & Biases and MLflow

objectives.text: - Integrate real-time experiment tracking tools (Weights & Biases, MLflow) into iterative training loops with minimal computational overhead.
- Log training and validation loss curves, evaluation accuracy, gradient norms, and learning rate schedules across continuous epochs.
- Structure hierarchical configuration dictionaries tracking all hyperparameters, random seeds, dataset versions, and model architectures.
- Log domain-specific research artifacts including generated validation samples, confusion matrices, and interactive attention heatmaps.
- Implement an automated checkpoint saving strategy saving best-validation models, periodic epoch states, and emergency recovery snapshots.
- Compare experiment runs across multi-dimensional parallel coordinate plots to isolate hyperparameter sensitivities and performance gains.

modules.mentalModel: An experiment tracker is a digital laboratory notebook capturing the exact relationship between configuration deltas and empirical outcomes.
modules.tryIt: Instrument a PyTorch training loop with Weights & Biases, logging scalar metrics, gradient norm histograms, and validation sample predictions.
modules.outcome: Systematically track hundreds of experimental runs, visualize metric trajectories, and maintain a centralized model registry.

modules.name: Hardware Determinism, Random Seeds & Scientific Data Loaders

objectives.text: - Identify hardware and software sources of numerical non-determinism in deep learning (CUDA atomic operations, cuDNN benchmarking, CPU threading).
- Implement deterministic initialization routines seeding Python random, NumPy, PyTorch CPU/GPU generators, and cuDNN deterministic flags.
- Understand the performance trade-offs of enabling torch.use_deterministic_algorithms() during initial prototyping versus large-scale runs.
- Build multi-worker PyTorch DataLoaders with custom worker initialization functions ensuring independent, deterministic worker random states.
- Avoid common multiprocessing pitfalls in PyTorch data loaders such as shared memory exhaustion, worker deadlocks, and duplicate augmentations.
- Implement memory-mapped dataset formats and pre-fetching pipelines (Arrow, WebDataset, HDF5) to prevent CPU data starvation during GPU training.

modules.mentalModel: True scientific reproducibility requires that rerunning a script with seed 42 produces identical bitwise loss values across epochs.
modules.tryIt: Write a deterministic seed utility function, verify that two independent training runs produce identical loss curves, and benchmark data loader throughput.
modules.outcome: Eliminate stochastic noise between runs, guarantee experimental determinism, and design high-throughput scientific data pipelines.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Reproducible Experiment Harness & Pipeline Template

objectives.text: - Design a modular, object-oriented experiment harness decoupling dataset loading, model architecture, training loop, and evaluation metrics.
- Implement structured configuration parsing with type validation and command-line overrides (Hydra, Pydantic, argparse).
- Create automated logging hooks capturing Git commit hash, environment diff, hardware specifications, and package versions at runtime start.
- Build a resilient training loop featuring automated checkpoint resumption, anomaly detection for NaN gradients, and graceful signal handling.
- Author an automated smoke-test suite verifying forward pass, backward gradient flow, and data pipeline throughput on dummy synthetic tensors.
- Package the harness into a reusable research template repository with complete documentation, container definition, and continuous integration.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Reproducible Experiment Harness & Pipeline Template

BRIEF: Build a standardized, publication-ready research scaffolding framework in PyTorch that guarantees bitwise reproducibility, tracks real-time experimental metrics, handles graceful checkpoint recovery, and exports complete environment provenance for academic code releases.
Build an experiment harness that:

- Parses hierarchical experiment configurations via structured configuration schemas with strict type validation and runtime command-line overrides.
- Logs scalar metrics, gradient norm distributions, learning rate schedules, and validation artifacts to Weights & Biases and local disk simultaneously.
- Detects NaN/Inf loss values and exploding gradients instantly, triggering informative debug dumps with tensor activation statistics.
- Implements atomic checkpoint saving with metadata sidecars recording validation metrics, optimizer states, learning rate schedules, and Git commit hashes.
- Automatically resumes interrupted training runs from the latest checkpoint without metric duplication or data epoch leakage.
- Features a unit test suite validating gradient propagation, deterministic outputs under fixed seeds, and data pipeline memory bounds.
Deliverables:

modules.mentalModel: A battle-tested research harness is a scientist's primary laboratory apparatus, reducing the time from new hypothesis to empirical result from weeks to hours.
modules.tryIt: Run the experiment harness with multiple configuration overrides, simulate a mid-training process termination, and verify seamless resumption from checkpoint.
modules.outcome: You can scaffold any machine learning research project with industrial-grade scientific rigor, guaranteed reproducibility, and frictionless collaboration.

levels.title: Research Problem Formulation, Mentorship & Lab Onboarding
levels.scope: Master the essential path of entering an active AI/ML research laboratory as an aspiring researcher: identifying active research groups and Principal Investigators (PIs), analyzing recent laboratory publications, formulating tailored research proposals, executing high-signal researcher outreach, passing technical Research Assistant (RA) screening, and establishing productive collaborative laboratory workflows.

modules.name: Mapping Research Laboratories, PIs & Active Research Trajectories

objectives.text: - Survey AI research institutes, national laboratories, and corporate research labs (e.g., DeepMind, Meta FAIR, Microsoft Research) in your area of interest.
- Inspect Principal Investigator (PI) profiles: evaluate recent grant funding (NSF, ERC, DARPA, NIH, industry gifts), student graduation records, and lab size.
- Analyze laboratory publication velocity: identify whether a lab publishes primarily in top-tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ACL, KDD) or specialized journals.
- Distinguish between advisory styles: hands-on junior group leaders versus hands-off senior research directors.
- Connect with current doctoral researchers and postdocs in the target lab to inquire about mentorship availability, computational resources, and project autonomy.
- Identify active multi-disciplinary collaborations (e.g., computer science labs collaborating with medical hospitals, oncology centers, or cybersecurity defense centers).

modules.mentalModel: Joining a lab is an intellectual apprenticeship; choosing a mentor who actively engages and has compute resources matters more than institutional branding.
modules.tryIt: Build a research spreadsheet profiling 10 research laboratories in your target domain, noting their PI, recent top-tier papers, active grants, and student ratio.
modules.outcome: Systematically identify high-impact research laboratories and select scientific mentors aligned with your research ambitions.

modules.name: Reading Laboratory Publications & Formulating Tailored Research Pitches

objectives.text: - Select the 3 most recent conference or journal papers published by the target PI and their senior doctoral researchers.
- Analyze the "Limitations and Future Work" sections of these papers to identify immediate, unresolved problems the lab is currently investigating.
- Formulate a precise understanding of the lab's technical stack, baseline benchmarks, and primary methodological paradigms.
- Develop a 1-page research pitch proposing a concrete extension or solution to an open problem identified in the lab’s recent work.
- Frame the pitch with clear benefits to the lab: how your technical skills (e.g., PyTorch engineering, CUDA profiling, dataset curation) can accelerate their active project.
- Connect the proposal to domain-specific datasets (e.g., applying their model to MIMIC-IV clinical records or network intrusion telemetry).

modules.mentalModel: A generic inquiry asks for an opportunity; a tailored research pitch demonstrates that you are already contributing solutions to their active problems.
modules.tryIt: Read two recent papers from a target research group, identify an unaddressed limitation, and write a concise 3-paragraph research extension proposal.
modules.outcome: Deconstruct prospective mentors' papers and formulate high-value research pitches that demonstrate immediate intellectual compatibility.

modules.name: High-Signal Research Outreach & Scientific Mentorship Proposals

objectives.text: - Analyze why research directors ignore 95% of generic student emails (lengthy generic CV dumps, copy-pasted flattery, vague requests for "any project").
objectives.group: The Anatomy of a High-Signal Cold Outreach

objectives.text: - Master the concise 4-paragraph email structure: who you are, specific citation of their recent work, proposed technical contribution, and polite call to action.
objectives.group: The Anatomy of a High-Signal Cold Outreach

objectives.text: - Craft professional, high-signal subject lines that stand out in crowded inboxes (e.g., "Prospective RA: Extending [Paper Title] with [Method]").
objectives.group: The Anatomy of a High-Signal Cold Outreach

objectives.text: - Optimize outreach timing around major conference submission deadlines (avoiding the week before NeurIPS/ICML submissions or major grant deadlines).
- Execute respectful, value-additive follow-up sequences after 7 to 10 days if no response is received, sharing a new insight or reproduction result.
- Leverage open scientific webinars, reading groups, and virtual workshops to initiate meaningful technical conversations.

modules.mentalModel: Research leads are starved for time but hungry for self-directed, technically capable researchers who take initiative without constant hand-holding.
modules.tryIt: Draft a 200-word cold outreach email to a target laboratory lead referencing a specific equation or figure from their latest paper, followed by a polite follow-up template.
modules.outcome: Author high-signal research outreach emails that secure technical interviews and avoid common applicant blunders.

modules.name: Developing an Academic Research CV & Demonstrating Technical Proof-of-Work

objectives.text: - Format a professional academic CV in LaTeX using clean typography (avoiding colorful graphic design templates used for corporate resumes).
- Structure standard academic sections: Education, Research Interests, Publications/Preprints, Research Experience, Open-Source Contributions, and Technical Skills.
- Highlight quantitative impact in past projects: benchmark scores, parameter scales, datasets curated, and reproducibility verification.
- Curate a research-oriented GitHub profile featuring clean reproductions of published papers, modular PyTorch implementations, and reproducible notebooks.
- Include interactive Weights & Biases experiment dashboards and Google Colab demonstrations directly linked from project README files.
- Document independent projects and exploratory studies as ArXiv-formatted technical reports rather than basic scripts.

modules.mentalModel: An academic CV establishes your credentials; a public, reproducible GitHub implementation provides indisputable proof of your research competence.
modules.tryIt: Typeset your academic CV in LaTeX using a clean academic template, linking a public GitHub repository that reproduces a published ML baseline.
modules.outcome: Build a stellar academic CV and proof-of-work portfolio that immediately distinguishes you from hundreds of applicant candidates.

modules.name: Passing the Research Assistant (RA) & Technical Lab Screening

objectives.text: - Prepare for standard lab screening technical rounds: live implementation of neural network layers, custom loss functions, and data pipelines in PyTorch.
- Demonstrate mastery of tensor manipulation: implementing batched matrix multiplication, Einstein summation (torch.einsum), and masking without loops.
- Debug deliberately corrupted models: diagnosing exploding gradients, dimension mismatches, and silent broadcasting errors in real time.
- Master the live paper presentation format: summarizing a assigned paper’s core hypothesis, mathematical derivation, and empirical limitations in 10 minutes.

objectives.text: - Defend against probing technical questions: explaining why the authors chose specific loss terms, baselines, or hyperparameter schedules.
objectives.group: Live Paper Discussion & Research Aptitude Interviews

objectives.text: - Articulate clear intellectual curiosity and resilience: discussing how you navigate dead-end experiments, negative results, and ambiguous research directions.

modules.outcome: Excel in technical coding evaluations and live paper defense discussions to secure coveted research positions.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Research Proposal & Laboratory Onboarding Portfolio

objectives.text: - Select a target research laboratory and synthesize their recent research trajectory into a comprehensive 3-page research proposal in LaTeX.
- Formulate 2 to 3 formal Research Questions (RQs) proposing a novel algorithmic extension, benchmark evaluation, or domain adaptation.

- Compile the complete application package: tailored 4-paragraph outreach email, LaTeX academic CV, 3-page research proposal, and GitHub portfolio links.
- Set up a clean, open-source reproduction repository demonstrating your ability to implement and benchmark a foundational baseline model.
- Conduct a peer review of the complete application package to verify professional tone, typographic elegance, and zero grammatical errors.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Research Proposal & Laboratory Onboarding Portfolio

Deliverables:

modules.mentalModel: A fully assembled research portfolio proves you are not merely looking for an opportunity, but are already prepared to execute publication-quality research on day one.
modules.tryIt: Assemble your complete application portfolio in LaTeX, linking a verified GitHub reproduction repository, and review against the rubric.
modules.outcome: You can systematically approach, pitch, and secure Research Assistant and Fellow positions at premier AI/ML research laboratories.

modules.name: Critical Paper Reading: The Three-Pass Method & Dissecting Scientific Claims

objectives.text: - Apply Keshav’s Three-Pass Method to evaluate paper relevance, understand main mechanisms, and dissect deep mathematical assumptions in structured tiers.
- Pass 1 (10 minutes): analyze title, abstract, section headings, and conclusions to determine if the paper is worth reading for your research question.
- Pass 2 (1 hour): grasp the paper's contents, analyze key figures and tables, and identify the core algorithmic contribution without getting bogged down in proofs.
- Pass 3 (multi-hour): mentally re-implement the paper from scratch, identifying implicit assumptions, unstated tricks, and missing baselines.
- Differentiate between rigorous theoretical proofs, validated empirical findings, and unsupported speculative claims.
- Identify common research red flags: cherry-picked qualitative examples, weak or un-tuned baselines, shifting metrics, and missing ablation tables.

modules.mentalModel: Reading an academic paper is not passive consumption; it is an active peer review where you cross-examine every claim against the empirical data.
modules.tryIt: Execute a 3-pass reading of a recent top-tier conference paper, writing a 1-page structured critique evaluating its core claims and baseline fairness.
modules.outcome: Read research papers efficiently, extract core insights rapidly, and critically evaluate the validity of scientific claims.

- Master BibTeX entry types: @article for journals, @inproceedings for conferences, @book for textbooks, and @misc for preprints.
- Maintain clean citation records: verify that ArXiv preprints are updated with official conference/journal publication citations once accepted.

modules.mentalModel: A disorganized researcher forgets 80% of what they read; an automated Zotero library turns reading into a searchable intellectual database.
modules.tryIt: Build a 30-paper library in Zotero with Better BibTeX keys, sync it to an Overleaf document, and cite three papers with formatted \cite{} commands.
modules.outcome: Manage thousands of scholarly references effortlessly, maintain pristine BibTeX registries, and streamline academic LaTeX authoring.

- Identify contradictory findings in published literature, isolating variations in dataset preprocessing or hyperparameter tuning as potential causes.
- Identify fertile research gaps: unaddressed failure modes, untested domain transfers (e.g., applying a vision technique to medical pathology), or scaling limits.

modules.outcome: Synthesize complex literature into comparative taxonomies, isolate significant research gaps, and frame scientific novelty compellingly.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Systematic Literature Survey (SLR) & PRISMA Flow Diagram

objectives.text: - Formulate a formal Systematic Literature Review (SLR) protocol following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews) guidelines.
- Define explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria, boolean search strings across 3 major databases, and screening procedures.
- Execute the search across databases, document raw results, remove duplicates, and record exclusion reasons across abstract and full-text screening.
- Construct a comprehensive comparative taxonomy matrix evaluating at least 25 screened papers across domain datasets, models, metrics, and limitations.
- Generate a formal PRISMA 2020 flow diagram illustrating the identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion stages.
- Author an academic Survey Paper manuscript in LaTeX (NeurIPS/IEEE format) detailing the state of the art, open challenges, and future research directions.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Systematic Literature Survey (SLR) & PRISMA Flow Diagram

The review must address an active research question in AI/ML (e.g., deep learning for medical diagnosis or graph neural networks for cybersecurity), evaluate at least 25 peer-reviewed papers, and construct a comprehensive taxonomy matrix.
Build a literature survey that:
- Formulates a clear research question (e.g., "What are the primary failure modes of transformer models in cyber threat detection?").
- Constructs structured boolean search queries across at least three major scholarly databases (e.g., IEEE Xplore, ACM DL, PubMed, ArXiv).
- Defines explicit inclusion criteria (e.g., peer-reviewed CORE A/A* conference or Q1 journal, empirical benchmark evaluated) and exclusion criteria.
- Implements a PRISMA 2020 flow diagram documenting the number of records identified, duplicates removed, abstracts screened, and final studies included.
- Builds a comprehensive comparative synthesis matrix evaluating all included papers across problem formulation, architecture, datasets, metrics, and limits.
- Constructs an original conceptual taxonomy diagram categorizing existing approaches into distinct algorithmic and architectural families.
- Synthesizes key open research gaps, emerging trends, and unaddressed challenges in the domain.
- Authors an 8-page academic Survey Paper in LaTeX following the standard IEEE Transactions or ACM Computing Surveys template with BibTeX citations.
Deliverables:
- Formally compiled 8-page Systematic Literature Review PDF in LaTeX.
- Vector graphics file of the PRISMA Flow Diagram and the conceptual taxonomy hierarchy.
- Complete Zotero/BibTeX library (.bib) containing cleanly formatted citations for all referenced works.
modules.mentalModel: A systematic literature review establishes you as an authoritative domain expert; it is often the first major publication of an MSc or PhD student.
modules.tryIt: Compile your complete SLR manuscript into a clean LaTeX PDF, complete with a PRISMA flow diagram, comparative taxonomy table, and 30+ BibTeX citations.
modules.outcome: You can systematically discover, critically analyze, and synthesize scientific literature to produce publication-grade survey papers and establish research authority.

objectives.text: - Calculate vector-valued partial derivatives, Jacobians, and gradient vectors for multi-layer composite matrix functions using multivariate chain rules.
- Connect symbolic multivariate calculus to algorithmic reverse-mode automatic differentiation (backpropagation) and vector-Jacobian products (VJPs).
- Formulate Taylor series approximations to first and second orders, analyzing local linearizations of complex non-linear loss surfaces.
- Derive the Hessian matrix of second-order partial derivatives and analyze its eigenvalues to evaluate local curvature (convexity, saddle points, ravines).
- Calculate the condition number of the Hessian to diagnose optimization pathologies such as ill-conditioned gradient oscillations.
- Understand empirical loss landscape visualization techniques (filter normalization, contour projections) used to analyze neural network trainability.

modules.mentalModel: The gradient indicates the direction of steepest ascent, while the Hessian eigenvalues determine whether the terrain is a flat basin, a steep ravine, or an unstable saddle point.
modules.tryIt: Compute the Hessian matrix of a non-linear loss function analytically and numerically, verify positive semi-definiteness, and compute its condition number.
modules.outcome: Analyze the geometric curvature of loss surfaces, derive custom matrix derivatives, and diagnose numerical optimization difficulties in deep learning models.

modules.name: Probability Distributions & Information-Theoretic Foundations

objectives.text: - Master parametric multivariate probability distributions: Gaussian, Bernoulli, Dirichlet, and categorical representations in generative and discriminative modeling.
- Derive Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) parameter estimates, linking priors directly to L1 (Laplace) and L2 (Gaussian) regularization.
- Analyze properties of exponential families, sufficiency, natural parameters, and log-partition functions in probabilistic graphical models.
- Derive Shannon Entropy, Conditional Entropy, and Mutual Information as formal measures of uncertainty and information transfer between random variables.
- Compute Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence and Jensen-Shannon Divergence, understanding asymmetry and zero-forcing versus zero-avoiding behaviors.
- Link Cross-Entropy loss directly to empirical KL divergence minimization in classification and language modeling tasks.

modules.mentalModel: Minimizing cross-entropy is mathematically equivalent to minimizing the KL divergence between true empirical data and your model's predicted distribution.
modules.tryIt: Implement KL divergence and Jensen-Shannon divergence between two multivariate Gaussian distributions and plot the divergence as variance parameters change.
modules.outcome: Apply formal information-theoretic metrics, formulate probabilistic model objectives, and interpret loss functions from first principles.

modules.name: Parametric & Non-Parametric Hypothesis Testing in ML Experiments

objectives.text: - Understand why reporting raw mean accuracy without hypothesis testing fails peer review standards in top-tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR).
- Test experimental result distributions for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk test, D'Agostino-Pearson omnibus test, and Q-Q normality plots.
- Apply Student's paired two-tailed t-test when normality assumptions hold, calculating test statistics, degrees of freedom, and two-tailed p-values.
- Understand why non-parametric tests are required when evaluating machine learning benchmarks with non-Gaussian, skewed, or bounded metric distributions.
- Execute the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired algorithmic comparisons across multiple benchmark datasets or cross-validation folds.
- Apply the Mann-Whitney U test for independent sample comparisons and the Friedman test with post-hoc Nemenyi tests for comparing multiple algorithms simultaneously.

modules.mentalModel: A p-value does not measure superiority; it measures how rarely you would observe such performance divergence if both algorithms were identical.
modules.tryIt: Take validation results from two model architectures across 10 random seeds, run Shapiro-Wilk tests for normality, and execute paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
modules.outcome: Select and execute appropriate parametric and non-parametric hypothesis tests to statistically validate performance improvements over baseline models.

modules.name: Effect Sizes, Confidence Intervals & Multiple Testing Correction

objectives.text: - Differentiate between statistical significance (low p-value) and practical scientific significance (meaningful performance gain in domain contexts).
- Calculate standardized effect size metrics: Cohen's d for parametric samples and Cliff's Delta or rank-biserial correlation for non-parametric comparisons.
- Implement empirical bootstrapping (10,000 resamples) to compute non-parametric 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) for complex evaluation metrics (e.g., F1, AUROC, BLEU).
- Understand the multiple comparison problem: running 20 independent statistical tests at alpha = 0.05 guarantees an expected false positive rate of 64%.
- Implement conservative family-wise error rate control using the Bonferroni correction and Holm-Bonferroni step-down adjustments.
- Apply False Discovery Rate (FDR) control using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for large-scale ablation studies and multi-metric benchmark evaluations.

modules.mentalModel: Reporting a 95% bootstrap confidence interval communicates both the magnitude of improvement and the empirical certainty of the measurement.
modules.tryIt: Write a Python utility that takes benchmark scores across 15 sub-tasks, computes Cohen's d effect sizes, and applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustments.
modules.outcome: Report effect sizes alongside confidence intervals and eliminate false positive claims caused by uncorrected multiple statistical comparisons.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Statistical Rigor & Hypothesis Testing Audit Package

objectives.group: Automated Significance Engine & Hypothesis Testing Pipeline

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Statistical Rigor & Hypothesis Testing Audit Package

BRIEF: Develop an automated, publication-ready Python statistical evaluation package that ingests benchmark results from multiple random seeds and baseline models, verifies distribution assumptions, computes parametric and non-parametric hypothesis tests, calculates bootstrap confidence intervals and effect sizes, and exports formatted LaTeX tables for academic submissions.
Build a statistical verification engine that:
- Ingests experimental result logs (e.g., accuracy, loss, F1, AUROC) across N random seeds for baseline and proposed methods.
- Performs automated normality screening using Shapiro-Wilk and Anderson-Darling tests, generating visual Q-Q plots.

Deliverables:

modules.mentalModel: Reviewers respect papers where every performance claim is backed by formal confidence intervals, effect sizes, and statistical hypothesis tests.
modules.tryIt: Execute the audit package on a simulated research experiment with 5 baselines and 10 seeds, generating a formatted LaTeX table ready for paper insertion.

levels.title: Dataset Discovery, Curation & Multi-Domain Adaptation
levels.scope: Master the discovery, ingestion, ethical curation, and preprocessing of real-world datasets across premier Computer Science research domains: medical/healthcare (MIMIC-IV EHR, CheXpert chest X-rays, TCGA genomic profiles), cybersecurity (CIC-IDS-2017 network traffic, Ember PE malware binaries, NSL-KDD), and scientific data; handling severe class imbalance, high missingness, patient/user privacy compliance (HIPAA, GDPR, de-identification), temporal data leakage prevention, and authoring formal "Datasheets for Datasets".

modules.name: Medical & Healthcare Datasets: MIMIC-IV, CheXpert & TCGA

objectives.text: - Complete human subjects research ethics training (CITI Program Data or Specimens Only Research) to secure credentialed access to PhysioNet and MIMIC-IV.
- Ingest and normalize relational electronic health records (EHR): ICD-9/10 diagnosis codes, clinical lab events, prescription tables, and ICU vital signs.
- Convert longitudinal patient admissions into standardized temporal event streams using medical ontology mappings (SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, LOINC).
- Process standard medical imaging formats (DICOM, NIfTI) for 2D chest radiographs (CheXpert, NIH ChestX-ray14) and 3D volumetric CT/MRI scans.
- Handle multi-label clinical radiology report uncertainty annotations (positive, negative, uncertain, unmentioned) via CheXpert labelers.
- Ingest The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) multimodal cohorts: aligning bulk RNA-seq gene expression profiles with clinical survival endpoints.

modules.mentalModel: Medical data represents human lives; strict privacy protocols and ontology alignment are essential before applying any machine learning model.
modules.tryIt: Download a de-identified sample of MIMIC-IV clinical events, map ICD-10 diagnostic codes to high-level clinical categories, and construct patient admission timelines.
modules.outcome: Acquire credentialed access to leading medical research databases and preprocess heterogeneous clinical, radiological, and genomic data.

modules.name: Cybersecurity & Threat Intelligence Datasets: CIC-IDS, Ember & PCAPs

objectives.text: - Parse raw network packet captures (PCAP) and bidirectional NetFlow / IPFIX flow records using Wireshark, Zeek, and Argus.
- Ingest modern intrusion detection datasets (CIC-IDS-2017, UNSW-NB15), analyzing simulated multi-stage attack scenarios (DDoS, PortScan, Infiltration, Brute Force).
- Extract statistical flow features: inter-arrival packet times, flow duration, byte volume ratios, and TCP flag anomalies.
- Ingest the Ember (Elastic Malware Benchmark for Empowering Researchers) and SOREL-20M benchmark datasets for Windows Portable Executable (PE) files.
- Extract static malware features: section table characteristics, imported DLL function calls, byte entropy histograms, and string metadata.
- Account for rapid concept drift in cybersecurity caused by evolving malware polymorphism and zero-day exploit campaigns over time.

modules.mentalModel: In cybersecurity research, adversaries actively adapt to evade detection; static benchmark distributions decay rapidly across temporal horizons.
modules.tryIt: Parse a raw PCAP file using Python Scapy, extract bidirectional flow statistics for benign and malicious traffic, and format feature vectors for ML ingestion.
modules.outcome: Process raw network packet captures and binary malware datasets, extracting domain-specific features for intrusion detection research.

modules.name: Handling Severe Class Imbalance & Real-World Missingness

objectives.text: - Understand the extreme rarity problem in medical pathology (rare diseases < 0.1%) and cybersecurity intrusion logs (attacks < 0.01% of total traffic).
- Compare sampling strategies: random minority over-sampling, Tomek link under-sampling, and synthetic oversampling via SMOTE and Borderline-SMOTE.
- Implement cost-sensitive learning and loss-function re-weighting: class-balanced focal loss, weighted cross-entropy, and LDAM (Label-Distribution-Aware Margin).
- Formalize missingness taxonomies: Missing Completely at Random (MCAR), Missing at Random (MAR), and Missing Not At Random (MNAR).
- Differentiate between informative clinical missingness (the absence of a lab test implies normal health) and sensor dropouts.
- Apply advanced imputation: Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and temporal forward-filling with missingness indicator masks.

modules.mentalModel: The fact that a clinical test or network sensor log was NOT recorded is itself a powerful predictive signal that must not be discarded.
modules.tryIt: Take an EHR dataset with 30% missing lab values, introduce missingness indicator masks, and compare MICE imputation against forward-fill baselines.
modules.outcome: Implement robust strategies to overcome extreme class imbalance and missing data without introducing distribution bias.

modules.name: Preventing Subtle Data Leakage & Temporal Contamination

objectives.text: - Identify catastrophic entity leakage: splitting multiple chest X-rays or ECG strips from the same patient across both training and test sets.
- Implement strict GroupKFold cross-validation partitioning data strictly at the patient ID or enterprise host level.
- Detect feature engineering leakage: fitting scalers, imputers, or dimensionality reduction transformations on the combined dataset prior to splitting.
- Identify temporal lookahead bias: predicting cyber attacks or patient sepsis using features calculated from future timestamps.
objectives.group: Temporal Contamination in Sequential & Security Data

objectives.text: - Implement rolling-origin temporal splits and PurgedGroupTimeSeriesSplit ensuring all test instances occur strictly after all training records.
objectives.group: Temporal Contamination in Sequential & Security Data

objectives.text: - Audit data preprocessing pipelines for target encoding leakage and subtle duplicate record contamination between train and test splits.
objectives.group: Temporal Contamination in Sequential & Security Data

modules.mentalModel: If your test split contains a single record from a patient or machine present in training, your published accuracy is an illusion.
modules.tryIt: Take a clinical dataset with multiple visits per patient, demonstrate the inflated performance of random splitting, and correct it using patient-level GroupKFold.
modules.outcome: Audit research pipelines to eliminate patient-level, feature engineering, and temporal data leakage that invalidates published research findings.

modules.name: Research Ethics, Data Governance & Datasheets for Datasets

objectives.text: - Master data privacy legal frameworks: HIPAA Safe Harbor and Expert Determination methods in the United States, and GDPR anonymization standards in the EU.
- Understand de-identification techniques: removing 18 HIPAA Direct Identifiers, date shifting by random patient offsets, and text scrubbing of unstructured clinical notes.
- Evaluate differential privacy (DP) guarantees: epsilon-delta budgets and noise addition mechanisms to protect against membership inference attacks.
- Adopt the "Datasheets for Datasets" framework (Gebru et al.) to document motivation, composition, collection process, preprocessing, uses, and distribution.
- Identify demographic, institutional, and geographical biases embedded in public medical (e.g., predominantly single-center hospital data) and cyber datasets.
- Author an ethical impact and broader impacts statement adhering to NeurIPS, ICML, and IEEE publication standards.

modules.mentalModel: A dataset without comprehensive provenance documentation is a black box that risks propagating harmful demographic bias and regulatory violations.
modules.tryIt: Author a formal 2-page Datasheet for Datasets document for an open-source medical or cybersecurity dataset, detailing collection protocols and known limitations.
modules.outcome: Comply with international privacy regulations, implement rigorous de-identification, and author academic Datasheets for Datasets.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Multi-Domain Research Dataset Curation & Benchmarking Pipeline

objectives.text: - Build an automated data engineering and curation pipeline targeting either a clinical cohort (MIMIC-IV / CheXpert) or a cybersecurity benchmark (CIC-IDS / Ember).
- Ingest raw heterogeneous data (relational tables, images, or packet flows), clean corrupted records, and implement entity-safe patient/host partitioning.
- Log missingness statistics, compute class distribution ratios, and verify that no feature leakage or temporal contamination occurs between splits.
- Implement domain-specific preprocessing: medical ontology normalization or network flow feature extraction with missingness indicator masks.
- Apply focal loss weighting or synthetic sampling to resolve severe class imbalance, maintaining a pristine, untouched test set.
- Package the curated benchmark into standardized PyTorch Dataset and DataLoader formats with comprehensive unit tests and automated integrity checks.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Multi-Domain Research Dataset Curation & Benchmarking Pipeline

BRIEF: Design and implement an end-to-end, publication-grade dataset curation and preprocessing pipeline for either clinical healthcare data (MIMIC-IV / CheXpert) or cybersecurity threat telemetry (CIC-IDS-2017 / Ember), enforcing strict entity-safe splitting, temporal leakage prevention, missingness modeling, and complete Datasheet documentation.
Build a data curation pipeline that:
- Ingests raw multi-modal or tabular data files, verifying checksum integrity and handling malformed records.
- Implements strict entity-level splitting (Patient ID or Network Host IP) to completely eliminate cross-set identity leakage.
- Enforces temporal train-validation-test ordering for sequential logs, preventing lookahead bias.
- Analyzes and documents missingness mechanisms, generating binary missingness indicator masks alongside robust imputations.
- Formulates class imbalance mitigation strategies (cost-sensitive weighting, focal loss parameters) calibrated on training splits only.
- Exports standardized PyTorch Dataset wrappers with deterministic caching and memory-mapped loading for fast GPU throughput.
- Generates an automated Data Quality & Hygiene Report detailing class distributions, correlation matrices, and leakage audit proofs.
Deliverables:
- Modular Python codebase (data_curation_pipeline/) with CLI interface and automated unit tests.
- Reproducible preprocessing scripts converting raw downloads into pristine, partitioned research artifacts.
- A comprehensive "Datasheet for Datasets" markdown document detailing dataset provenance, ethical considerations, and known biases.
- Interactive visualization dashboard displaying feature distributions, missingness patterns, and class imbalance ratios across splits.
modules.mentalModel: High-impact AI/ML research begins with pristine, leak-free data curation; a flawless benchmark pipeline provides the foundation for valid scientific discoveries.
modules.tryIt: Run the full curation pipeline end-to-end on raw data, verifying zero patient overlap and exporting a complete metadata manifest.
modules.outcome: You can ingest, sanitize, partition, and document complex domain-specific research datasets with zero data leakage, ready for peer-reviewed publication.

levels.title: Classical Machine Learning & Deep Learning Paradigms
levels.scope: Systematically explore foundational and deep learning modeling paradigms across domains: comparing tree ensembles (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) against deep tabular models (TabNet) on clinical and cybersecurity tabular records, spatial representation learning via 2D/3D Convolutional Neural Networks (3D U-Net, ResNet, Med3D) for volumetric medical imaging (CT/MRI), 1D CNNs and recurrent networks for temporal intrusion logs, transfer learning, and domain adaptation.

modules.name: Tabular Modeling Paradigms: Gradient Boosted Trees vs Deep Tabular

objectives.text: - Master the mathematical foundations of gradient tree boosting: second-order Taylor expansion of the loss function, split finding algorithms, and leaf weight shrinkage.
objectives.group: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM & CatBoost)

objectives.text: - Apply XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost to tabular clinical records (MIMIC-IV patient mortality prediction) and cybersecurity logs (CIC-IDS attack classification).
objectives.group: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM & CatBoost)

objectives.text: - Handle categorical features natively using target encoding, frequency encoding, and CatBoost's ordered target statistics to prevent target leakage.
objectives.group: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (XGBoost, LightGBM & CatBoost)

objectives.text: - Implement deep architectures tailored for tabular data: TabNet (sequential sparse attention masks) and Feature Tokenizer Transformer (FT-Transformer).
- Compare inductive biases: understand why GBDTs consistently outperform standard multi-layer perceptrons on unrotated heterogeneous tabular data.
- Benchmark training compute, inference throughput, and hyperparameter sensitivity between tree ensembles and deep tabular models.

modules.mentalModel: GBDTs partition feature space along orthogonal hyperplanes, making them the gold-standard baseline for non-spatial, unrotated tabular data.
modules.tryIt: Train an XGBoost baseline and a TabNet model on a clinical tabular dataset, comparing AUROC, parameter count, and training wall-clock time.
modules.outcome: Select, tune, and evaluate state-of-the-art tree ensembles and deep tabular models across medical and cybersecurity benchmarks.

modules.name: Spatial Deep Learning & Medical Imaging: 2D/3D CNNs & U-Net

objectives.text: - Analyze inductive biases of convolutional operators: translation equivariance, weight sharing, and localized receptive field hierarchies.
objectives.group: Convolutional Backbones & Spatial Invariance (ResNet to ConvNeXt)

objectives.text: - Implement residual learning (ResNet), grouped convolutions (ResNeXt), and modernized architectures (ConvNeXt) for 2D radiological images (CheXpert).
objectives.group: Convolutional Backbones & Spatial Invariance (ResNet to ConvNeXt)

objectives.text: - Evaluate receptive field expansion, multi-scale feature pyramids (FPN), and global average pooling for multi-label pathological classification.
objectives.group: Convolutional Backbones & Spatial Invariance (ResNet to ConvNeXt)

objectives.text: - Transition from 2D pixel grids to 3D voxel grids for volumetric medical imaging (CT and MRI scans from the Medical Segmentation Decathlon).
- Architect the 3D U-Net: encoder feature compression, skip connections preserving high-resolution spatial boundaries, and decoder upsampling.
- Formulate specialized segmentation loss functions: Soft Dice Loss, Generalized Dice Loss, and Focal Tversky Loss to handle severe foreground-background voxel imbalance.

modules.mentalModel: Skip connections in U-Net act as spatial bridges, allowing fine-grained anatomical edge details to bypass the bottleneck directly to the decoder.
modules.tryIt: Implement a 3D U-Net in PyTorch, apply Soft Dice Loss on a volumetric brain tumor segmentation dataset, and compute the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC).
modules.outcome: Design and train 2D and 3D convolutional neural networks for medical radiological classification and volumetric anatomical segmentation.

modules.name: Temporal & Sequential Paradigms: 1D CNNs, BiLSTMs & TCNs

objectives.text: - Apply 1D temporal convolutions to sequential telemetry data: continuous ICU physiological waveforms (ECG, arterial blood pressure) and network packet bursts.
- Architect Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN): causal convolutions preventing future leakage and dilated convolutions providing exponentially expanding receptive fields.
- Analyze computational advantages of TCNs over recurrent networks: massively parallel training execution and stable gradient propagation across long time horizons.
- Derive the mathematical gating equations for Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), analyzing how additive cell state updates mitigate vanishing gradients.
- Train Bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTM) with temporal attention mechanisms on cybersecurity log sequences and sequential clinical lab event histories.
- Compare sequential modeling performance: evaluate memory footprint, sequential inference latency, and temporal context retention across 1D CNNs and LSTMs.

modules.mentalModel: Dilated causal convolutions expand receptive field exponentially without increasing parameter count, offering a parallelizable alternative to recurrence.
modules.tryIt: Build a Temporal Convolutional Network with dilated causal residual blocks in PyTorch, training it on raw network packet sequence data to detect intrusion anomalies.
modules.outcome: Model time-series physiological waveforms and sequential cybersecurity telemetry using 1D convolutional and recurrent deep learning architectures.

modules.name: Self-Supervised Representation Learning across Domains

objectives.text: - Formulate contrastive representation learning from first principles: the InfoNCE loss function and positive/negative pair formulation.
- Implement SimCLR and Momentum Contrast (MoCo) frameworks, analyzing the role of memory banks, momentum encoders, and temperature hyperparameters.
- Design domain-specific data augmentations: random cropping, Gaussian blur, and affine transformations for medical scans; random jitter and masking for cyber telemetry.
- Analyze non-contrastive self-supervised architectures (Barlow Twins, BYOL) that eliminate negative pairs by minimizing cross-correlation redundancy.
objectives.group: Non-Contrastive & Masked Representation Learning (Barlow Twins & MAE)

objectives.text: - Implement Masked Autoencoders (MAE): masking 75% of input visual or spatial patches and training lightweight decoders to reconstruct pixel intensities.
objectives.group: Non-Contrastive & Masked Representation Learning (Barlow Twins & MAE)

objectives.text: - Evaluate learned representations using linear probing (freezing the backbone and training a linear classifier) and k-nearest-neighbors evaluation.
objectives.group: Non-Contrastive & Masked Representation Learning (Barlow Twins & MAE)

modules.mentalModel: Self-supervised learning exploits massive unlabeled datasets to build rich geometric representation spaces before a single task-specific label is seen.
modules.tryIt: Pre-train a convolutional encoder using SimCLR on unlabelled chest X-rays, freeze the backbone, and evaluate linear probe classification accuracy against supervised training.
modules.outcome: Pre-train domain-specific visual and sequential encoders using self-supervised contrastive and reconstruction objectives without manual labels.

modules.name: Transfer Learning, Domain Shift & Out-of-Distribution Generalization

objectives.text: - Master transfer learning mechanics: layer freezing, discriminative learning rates, gradual unfreezing, and feature extraction vs. full fine-tuning.
- Investigate negative transfer: when pre-training on natural images (ImageNet) provides suboptimal representations for specialized domains (microscopy or packet flows).
- Apply domain adaptation techniques: Domain Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) using gradient reversal layers (GRL) to align source and target latent spaces.
- Formalize distribution shift: covariate shift (P(X) shifts while P(Y|X) is constant), concept drift (P(Y|X) shifts), and label shift (P(Y) shifts).
- Evaluate multi-center domain generalization in healthcare: training a diagnostic model on Hospital A and testing zero-shot generalization on Hospital B and C.
- Stress-test cybersecurity classifiers against temporal concept drift: evaluating malware classifiers on binaries compiled months or years after the training window.

modules.mentalModel: High within-distribution test accuracy is easy; true scientific robustness requires generalization across different hospitals, scanner protocols, and enterprise networks.
modules.tryIt: Train a classifier on data from one institution, test on a secondary institution to measure out-of-distribution performance drop, and mitigate the drop using DANN.
modules.outcome: Detect and mitigate domain shift, evaluate out-of-distribution generalization, and apply transfer learning across distinct scientific environments.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Cross-Paradigm Clinical & Cybersecurity Modeling Benchmark

objectives.text: - Build an end-to-end comparative benchmarking framework implementing classical tree ensembles (LightGBM/XGBoost), deep tabular models (TabNet), and deep neural networks.
- Evaluate on both a clinical risk prediction task (MIMIC-IV mortality/sepsis) and a cybersecurity threat detection task (CIC-IDS-2017 intrusion classification).
- Standardize evaluation protocols: compute-matched hyperparameter tuning, identical cross-validation folds, and unified evaluation metric logging.
- Compute multi-dimensional metrics: AUROC, AUPRC (Average Precision), Expected Calibration Error (ECE), parameter count, and inference latency per sample.
- Execute paired statistical hypothesis tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank) to determine whether deep learning outperforms tree ensembles with statistical significance.
- Generate publication-ready comparative tables and ROC/PR curve plots formatted for conference submission.

modules.mentalModel: Rigorous research avoids paradigm dogmatism; systematically comparing classical and deep models on equal footing reveals genuine empirical trade-offs.

levels.title: Sequence Models, Graph Neural Networks & Transformers
levels.scope: Investigate modern representation architectures across complex relational and sequential data: self-attention mechanisms, Vision Transformers (ViT) and Swin Transformers, Graph Neural Networks (GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE) for cybersecurity threat graphs (botnet detection, binary function call graphs) and molecular interactions, and linear attention/state space models (Mamba, S4) for long-sequence genomic and network telemetry modeling.
levels.prereqStated: Level 5 (Classical Machine Learning & Deep Learning Paradigms)

modules.name: Self-Attention Mechanics & the Modern Transformer

objectives.text: - Derive scaled dot-product attention from first principles: query, key, value matrix projections, softmax scaling factors, and attention dispersion.
- Implement multi-head attention (MHA), Multi-Query Attention (MQA), and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), analyzing KV-cache memory reductions.
- Compare positional encodings: absolute sinusoidal encodings, learned positional embeddings, ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases), and Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE).
- Analyze the quadratic computational and memory complexity O(N^2) of standard attention with respect to sequence length N.
- Master the IO-awareness principles of FlashAttention (Dao et al.): tiling matrices across fast GPU SRAM to avoid high-bandwidth memory (HBM) memory bandwidth bottlenecks.
- Implement causal attention masking, padding masks, and document packing for efficient variable-length sequence batching.

modules.mentalModel: Standard attention is memory-bandwidth bound, not compute-bound; FlashAttention reorganizes matrix multiplications to fit within fast on-chip GPU SRAM.
modules.tryIt: Implement scaled dot-product attention in PyTorch from scratch, verify output equivalence with torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention, and benchmark memory scaling.
modules.outcome: Build, optimize, and mathematically analyze modern attention mechanisms and hardware-aware Transformer layers.

modules.name: Vision Transformers & Hierarchical Attention in Medical Imaging

objectives.text: - Transition Transformers to 2D spatial domains: non-overlapping patch extraction, linear projection to 1D patch tokens, and prependable [CLS] tokens.
- Analyze inductive bias differences: why ViTs require large-scale pre-training compared to CNNs due to the absence of translation equivariance and locality biases.
- Implement attention map rollouts and Grad-CAM for Vision Transformers to visualize clinical attention on thoracic lesions.
- Architect the Swin Transformer: hierarchical feature representation via patch merging and shifted local window self-attention with linear computational complexity.
- Apply Swin-UNETR and hybrid Transformer-CNN architectures to 3D volumetric medical segmentation and gigapixel whole-slide histopathology images (WSI).
- Analyze multi-scale attention mechanisms for resolving both fine-grained cellular features and global organ-level context simultaneously.

modules.mentalModel: ViTs treat images as sentences of visual words; Swin Transformers reintroduce hierarchical spatial pyramids while maintaining attention flexibility.
modules.tryIt: Implement a patch embedding module in PyTorch, construct a Vision Transformer backbone, and visualize attention weights across a medical chest X-ray image.
modules.outcome: Apply Vision Transformers and hierarchical attention models to medical radiological imaging and high-resolution spatial data.

modules.name: Graph Neural Networks: Message Passing, GCN & GAT

objectives.text: - Formalize graph-structured data: node feature matrices, edge index adjacency lists, and edge attribute tensors using PyTorch Geometric (PyG).
objectives.group: The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) Framework

objectives.text: - Formulate the general Message Passing framework: neighborhood message aggregation, message transformation, and node state update functions.
objectives.group: The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) Framework

objectives.text: - Analyze the theoretical expressive limits of message-passing GNNs: the 1-dimensional Weisfeiler-Lehman (1-WL) graph isomorphism test.
objectives.group: The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) Framework

objectives.text: - Implement Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) via localized first-order spectral approximations of graph Laplacians.
- Implement Graph Attention Networks (GAT): calculating learnable anisotropic attention coefficients between neighboring nodes.

modules.mentalModel: A GNN is a generalized convolution where each node dynamically aggregates information from its arbitrary topological neighborhood.
modules.tryIt: Build a 2-layer Graph Attention Network (GAT) with multi-head neighborhood attention in PyTorch Geometric, training it on a node classification benchmark.
modules.outcome: Master the Message Passing paradigm and implement state-of-the-art spatial and attention-based Graph Neural Networks.

modules.name: Graph Neural Networks for Cybersecurity & Complex Threat Topologies

objectives.text: - Represent cybersecurity telemetry as directed property graphs: network communication graphs (IP to IP), host authentication graphs, and system provenance logs.
- Detect coordinated botnet command-and-control (C2) topologies using GNN node and edge classification on large-scale network flow graphs.
- Handle dynamic and temporal graphs: incorporating edge timestamps, packet volumes, and protocol features into continuous-time dynamic graph networks (TGN).
- Disassemble compiled malicious binaries into Control Flow Graphs (CFG) and Abstract Syntax Trees (AST) using Ghidra or radare2.
- Train Graph Convolutional Networks on function-level CFGs to classify malware families and detect obfuscated zero-day exploit variants.
- Mitigate graph oversmoothing and oversquashing when message passing traverses deep multi-hop dependency chains in large computer networks.

modules.mentalModel: Cyber threats operate across distributed networks; graph neural networks capture relational attack topologies invisible to isolated log analyzers.
modules.tryIt: Construct an enterprise network communication graph from network flow logs in PyG, train a GNN to detect compromised lateral-movement host nodes.
modules.outcome: Formulate cybersecurity threat detection problems as graph neural network tasks, modeling network flow graphs and malware binary control flow topologies.

modules.name: State Space Models & Long-Sequence Architectures (Mamba & S4)

objectives.text: - Analyze the quadratic bottleneck of Transformers when processing ultra-long sequences (e.g., millions of base pairs in genomics or continuous network traffic).
- Formalize linear continuous-time State Space Models (SSMs): mapping continuous 1D inputs to outputs through latent continuous hidden states.
- Discretize continuous state spaces using the bilinear transform and the HiPPO (High-order Polynomial Projection Operators) framework for optimal memory initialization.
- Implement Mamba (Gu & Dao): introducing input-dependent, selective parameters into the state space matrices (B, C, and step size Delta).
objectives.group: Selective State Spaces: The Mamba Architecture

objectives.text: - Master the hardware-aware selective scan algorithm: computing linear recurrent updates via an associative parallel scan directly in GPU SRAM.
objectives.group: Selective State Spaces: The Mamba Architecture

objectives.text: - Evaluate Mamba on long-context sequence benchmarks: comparing token throughput, memory footprint, and sequence extrapolation against FlashAttention Transformers.
objectives.group: Selective State Spaces: The Mamba Architecture

modules.mentalModel: Mamba achieves the parallel training efficiency of Transformers and the constant-memory O(1) inference speed of recurrent neural networks.
modules.tryIt: Implement a 1D selective state space layer in PyTorch, compare training wall-clock time and memory consumption against standard attention across sequence length N=16,384.
modules.outcome: Apply sub-quadratic linear attention and selective state space models (Mamba) to long-sequence scientific and telemetry data.

levels.title: Generative Modeling & Probabilistic Machine Learning
levels.scope: Master probabilistic and generative models for data synthesis, density estimation, and anomaly detection: Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM), score-based generative modeling, and Continuous Flow Matching (CFM); generating privacy-preserving synthetic clinical cohorts (MIMIC-IV) and synthetic cybersecurity attack vectors; evaluating generative fidelity and diversity via Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Precision & Recall for Generative Models, and membership inference vulnerability.
levels.prereqStated: Level 6 (Sequence Models, Graph Neural Networks & Transformers)

modules.name: Latent Variable Models & Variational Autoencoders (VAEs)

objectives.text: - Formulate continuous latent variable models: the intractable marginal likelihood p(x) and variational posterior approximation q(z|x).
- Derive the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) from Jensen's inequality and KL divergence, separating reconstruction loss from latent prior regularization.
- Implement the reparameterization trick (z = mu + sigma * epsilon) allowing low-variance reverse-mode gradient backpropagation through stochastic nodes.
- Analyze beta-VAE: balancing reconstruction fidelity against latent factor disentanglement and addressing catastrophic posterior collapse.
- Implement Conditional VAEs (C-VAE) conditioned on clinical diagnostic labels or cybersecurity network attack categories.
- Generate synthetic mixed-type tabular clinical records (continuous vitals + discrete diagnosis codes) using categorical Gumbel-Softmax relaxations.

modules.mentalModel: The reparameterization trick isolates the stochastic sampling into an external noise parameter, enabling end-to-end gradient flow.
modules.tryIt: Implement a Conditional VAE in PyTorch, train it on mixed-type tabular records, and generate synthetic samples conditioned on specific disease labels.
modules.outcome: Derive the ELBO, implement the reparameterization trick, and generate conditioned tabular samples using Variational Autoencoders.

modules.name: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM & Score Matching)

objectives.text: - Formalize the forward discrete-time Markovian diffusion process: gradually corrupting clean data x_0 into isotropic Gaussian noise via a variance schedule beta_t.
- Derive the closed-form sampling equation for arbitrary timestep t without iterative stepping (x_t as a linear combination of x_0 and standard Gaussian noise).
- Train a reverse denoising U-Net predicting the injected noise epsilon_theta under a simplified mean-squared error objective (Ho et al.).
- Connect DDPM to score-based generative modeling (Song & Ermon): learning the gradient of the log probability density (the Stein score function) at multiple noise scales.
- Formulate diffusion as continuous Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs): Variance Preserving (VP) and Variance Exploding (VE) SDEs.
- Sample from reverse SDEs and Probability Flow ODEs using Euler-Maruyama numerical solvers and predictor-corrector algorithms.

modules.mentalModel: Diffusion reverses entropy; by training a neural network to predict noise at every scale, we can trace a trajectory from pure noise back to the data manifold.
modules.tryIt: Train a 2D Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) on a radiological imaging dataset in PyTorch, implementing the full reverse sampling loop.
modules.outcome: Master the mathematics of discrete and continuous diffusion, train denoising backbones, and generate high-fidelity samples from pure noise.

modules.name: Continuous Normalizing Flows & Optimal Transport Flow Matching

objectives.text: - Master continuous-time invertible models: mapping base Gaussian densities to complex target data distributions via Neural ODEs (Chen et al.).
objectives.group: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations & Continuous Flows

objectives.text: - Compute exact log-likelihoods using the instantaneous change-of-variables formula and Hutchinson's trace estimator for scalable Jacobian trace computation.
objectives.group: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations & Continuous Flows

objectives.text: - Contrast the straight-line paths of continuous flows against the curved, stochastic trajectories of Brownian motion in standard diffusion.
objectives.group: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations & Continuous Flows

objectives.text: - Implement Flow Matching (Lipman et al.): regressing time-dependent vector fields directly without costly numerical ODE simulation during training.
- Apply Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM): establishing straight-line probability paths between noise distributions and data points.
- Benchmark inference speed: generating high-fidelity samples in as few as 10-20 deterministic Euler steps, drastically outperforming standard DDPM sampling.

modules.mentalModel: Flow matching straightens the generative trajectories into straight lines, enabling dramatically faster deterministic sampling with fewer ODE solver steps.
modules.tryIt: Implement an Optimal Transport Flow Matching model in PyTorch on a 2D synthetic dataset, visualize the learned velocity vector fields, and integrate trajectories.
modules.outcome: Formulate continuous normalizing flows and implement Optimal Transport Flow Matching for fast, deterministic generative sampling.

modules.name: Domain-Specific Generative Synthesis: Medical Scans & Cyber Telemetry

- Synthesize realistic rare pathological lesions (e.g., glioblastoma brain tumors on MRI) to augment severely data-scarce medical training splits.
- Perform lesion inpainting and counterfactual image generation: modifying specific anatomical regions while preserving patient-specific identity features.
- Generate realistic, synthetic bidirectional network flow telemetry mimicking stealthy advanced persistent threat (APT) multi-stage attack campaigns.
- Synthesize functional polymorphic malware feature vectors that mimic benign Windows PE executables to test intrusion detection evasion.
- Ensure format-preserving constraints: enforcing protocol validities, packet size limits, and non-negative integer counts in synthetic network traces.

modules.mentalModel: Generative models can solve extreme domain data scarcity by synthesizing high-fidelity, physically consistent rare pathological lesions and cyber threats.
modules.tryIt: Train a conditioned diffusion model to synthesize realistic rare pathology samples, and verify that training a downstream classifier with augmented data improves AUROC.
modules.outcome: Deploy state-of-the-art diffusion and flow models to synthesize high-utility medical images and cybersecurity telemetry.

modules.name: Generative Evaluation Metrics, Fidelity & Privacy Auditing

objectives.text: - Compute Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) to quantify distributional distance between real and synthetic feature embeddings extracted from pre-trained backbones.
objectives.group: Sample Quality & Diversity Metrics (FID, Precision & Recall)

objectives.text: - Decompose generative performance into Precision (fidelity of generated samples) and Recall (diversity and coverage of the target distribution) (Sajjadi et al.).
objectives.group: Sample Quality & Diversity Metrics (FID, Precision & Recall)

objectives.text: - Evaluate domain-specific realism: clinical radiological feature preservation evaluated by domain experts, and packet header validity checks for cyber telemetry.
objectives.group: Sample Quality & Diversity Metrics (FID, Precision & Recall)

objectives.text: - Understand the privacy risks of synthetic data: generative models can memorize and regurgitate individual training records, violating HIPAA or GDPR.
- Execute Membership Inference Attacks (MIA): training shadow models to determine whether a specific patient record was present in the generative training set.
- Quantify attribute disclosure risks and evaluate Differentially Private Diffusion (DP-Diffusion) using Rényi Differential Privacy accounting.

modules.mentalModel: High visual fidelity is meaningless if the generative model simply memorized and reproduced confidential patient scans; privacy auditing is mandatory.
modules.tryIt: Calculate FID, Precision, and Recall on synthetic samples, and implement a shadow-model membership inference attack to verify that training patient data is not leaked.
modules.outcome: Evaluate generative fidelity, diversity, and distributional realism, and conduct empirical privacy audits to prevent training data memorization.
