modules.mentalModel: The ultimate test of synthetic data research is downstream clinical or security utility combined with mathematical privacy guarantees.
modules.tryIt: Run the full synthesis pipeline, train a downstream model on synthetic data, evaluate on real test data, and produce a publication-ready evaluation report.
modules.outcome: You can design, train, evaluate, and mathematically audit state-of-the-art generative diffusion and flow models for sensitive scientific and enterprise domains.

levels.title: Experimental Design, Ablation Studies & Fair Benchmarking
levels.scope: Master the scientific method of empirical computer science experimentation: designing multi-factor ablation studies (One-Factor-At-A-Time and factorial grids), isolating independent from confounding variables, establishing compute-matched and parameter-matched baselines, detecting benchmark data leakage and train-test contamination, implementing fair hyperparameter sweeps under fixed compute budgets, and formatting publication-grade comparative tables.

modules.name: Controlled Experiments: Independent, Dependent & Confounding Variables

objectives.text: - Formulate precise, falsifiable scientific hypotheses: stating the exact mechanism by which a proposed architectural modification or loss term improves performance.
- Strictly define independent variables (e.g., custom attention gating, novel regularization) and dependent variables (AUROC, task accuracy, inference latency).
- Identify and isolate confounding variables that secretly drive performance gains: hidden optimizer learning rate tuning, different batch schedules, and warmups.
- Enforce strict parameter-matched and compute-matched experimental controls when comparing a novel architecture against established baselines.
- Calculate and report total training floating-point operations (FLOPs) using standard 6*N*D approximations to ensure gains do not stem purely from scale.
- Normalize hardware variables: evaluating all competing models on identical GPU architectures (e.g., NVIDIA A100/H100) under identical numerical precision (BF16).

modules.mentalModel: If your model outperforms the baseline simply because it had 25% more parameters or a longer warmup schedule, your scientific claim is invalid.
modules.tryIt: Design an experimental protocol comparing two attention mechanisms where total parameter count, FLOP budget, and training token count are strictly equalized.
modules.outcome: Structure scientifically controlled computer science experiments that isolate genuine algorithmic contributions from confounding factors.

modules.name: Ablation Study Design: Component Isolation & Negative Controls

objectives.text: - Understand the primary purpose of an ablation study: demonstrating that every proposed component is strictly necessary and operates as hypothesized.
- Design One-Factor-At-A-Time (OFAT) and 2^k full factorial ablation grids that systematically remove or substitute individual algorithmic modules.
- Formulate component-level ablations: testing custom loss penalties, normalization layers, positional encodings, and data filtering thresholds.
- Implement random ablation baselines: replace learned modules with random fixed projections or identity mappings to measure actual learned contributions.
- Execute feature permutation and feature ablation tests to verify that model performance degrades when critical input signals are corrupted.
- Structure ablation tables in scientific papers with progressive rows showing performance drops as each novel component is stripped away.

modules.mentalModel: An ablation study is an empirical post-mortem showing the exact quantitative degradation incurred when any piece of your innovation is removed.
modules.tryIt: Construct an ablation matrix for a model with three new components (loss penalty, novel attention, custom normalization), detailing all 2^3 configurations.
modules.outcome: Design rigorous ablation matrices that withstand peer review scrutiny and scientifically justify every architectural design choice.

modules.name: Baseline Selection: Fair Comparisons & the Weak Baseline Fallacy

objectives.text: - Select state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines, canonical historical architectures, and simple heuristic baselines to establish meaningful performance bounds.
- Avoid the "weak baseline" trap: ensure published baseline implementations are tuned with identical diligence and compute resources as the proposed method.
- Re-run baselines in your own standardized experimental codebase rather than copying numbers from prior papers evaluated under different protocols.
- Define what constitutes a genuine "State of the Art" (SOTA) claim and when to state nuanced findings instead of sweeping superiority claims.
- Report all failure modes and negative results transparently: identify scenarios where the proposed method underperforms established baselines.
- Document hyperparameter search spaces and selection criteria for all baselines in the supplementary material to ensure full reproducibility.

modules.mentalModel: Reviewers will instantly reject a paper that claims superiority over an untuned, outdated, or strawman baseline.
modules.tryIt: Re-implement a published baseline model, tune its hyperparameters on your target dataset, and compare the tuned baseline against default settings.
modules.outcome: Select, tune, and evaluate competitive baseline models, eliminating the weak-baseline fallacy from your research papers.

modules.name: Benchmark De-Contamination & Evaluation Integrity

objectives.text: - Understand the contamination crisis in modern AI: pre-trained foundation models inadvertently memorizing public benchmark test sets during pre-training.
objectives.group: Detecting Data Contamination in Pre-Trained Models

objectives.text: - Implement n-gram overlap filtering (e.g., 8-gram or 13-gram exact matches) between pre-training corpora and evaluation benchmark sets.
objectives.group: Detecting Data Contamination in Pre-Trained Models

objectives.text: - Execute embedding-based semantic similarity searches to detect paraphrased or synthetically altered test set instances present in training data.
objectives.group: Detecting Data Contamination in Pre-Trained Models

objectives.text: - Construct dynamic, time-split evaluation sets that cannot exist in static pre-training corpora (e.g., clinical cases or cyber attacks recorded post-cutoff).
- Implement canary strings and digital watermarks in proprietary evaluation datasets to automatically detect web scraping and training contamination.
- Report decontaminated evaluation metrics: showing model performance before and after removing contaminated test instances.

modules.mentalModel: Testing a model on data it has already seen during pre-training is not an evaluation of generalization; it is an evaluation of memorization.
modules.tryIt: Scan an evaluation benchmark against a simulated pre-training text corpus using n-gram overlap matching, identify contaminated samples, and compute decontaminated accuracy.
modules.outcome: Detect and eliminate benchmark test-set contamination, ensuring evaluation integrity in foundation model research.

modules.name: Hyperparameter Tuning Protocols & Resource Allocation

objectives.text: - Compare search strategies: grid search, random search, and Bayesian optimization via Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE in Optuna).
- Establish fixed compute budgets: allocating equal numbers of GPU hours or training trials to both proposed methods and baseline models.
- Implement early stopping and multi-fidelity optimization (Asynchronous Successive Halving Algorithm ASHA) to prune unpromising trial configurations.
- Train the best hyperparameter configuration across at least 5 to 10 distinct random seeds to quantify stochastic optimization variance.
- Report complete distribution statistics: mean, standard deviation, median, and interquartile range (IQR) for all primary benchmark metrics.
- Analyze hyperparameter sensitivity: plotting performance surfaces across learning rate, weight decay, and dropout sweeps to prove robustness.

modules.mentalModel: An algorithm that achieves peak performance only on a single magical random seed is a fragile artifact, not a scientific contribution.
modules.tryIt: Run an Optuna Bayesian hyperparameter sweep across learning rates and weight decays under a fixed 20-trial budget, then evaluate the best model across 5 random seeds.
modules.outcome: Implement disciplined hyperparameter optimization protocols with equal compute budgets and report multi-seed variance.

modules.name: Capstone Project: Comprehensive Ablation Study & Empirical Benchmarking Suite

objectives.text: - Build a publication-ready empirical benchmarking suite comparing your proposed research method against at least three competitive baselines.
- Target a concrete domain benchmark: clinical patient mortality risk (MIMIC-IV) or network intrusion detection (CIC-IDS-2017).
- Enforce strict compute-matched hyperparameter sweeps, parameter count alignment, and identical evaluation data splits.
- Execute a full factorial ablation study systematically isolating each novel component (loss terms, architectural modules, preprocessing steps).
- Run all configurations across 5 random seeds, computing mean, standard deviation, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, and paired Wilcoxon tests.
- Automatically generate publication-quality LaTeX comparative tables and multi-factor ablation bar plots formatted for conference submission.

notes: CAPSTONE PROJECT: Comprehensive Ablation Study & Empirical Benchmarking Suite

BRIEF: Design, execute, and document a publication-grade empirical benchmarking study and multi-factor ablation experiment comparing a novel research architecture against three tuned baselines on a real-world domain dataset, adhering to strict compute-matched budgets and statistical rigor.
Build an empirical benchmarking harness that:
- Implements a proposed research architecture alongside three competitive, well-tuned baseline models.
- Enforces strict compute-matched parameter sweeps (Optuna TPE) under an identical fixed trial budget across all models.
- Conducts a 2^k full factorial ablation study systematically toggling individual architectural components, loss terms, and normalizations.
- Executes all top configurations across 5 independent random seeds with fixed seed propagation.
- Calculates comprehensive metrics: performance scores, parameter counts, training FLOPs, peak VRAM, and inference throughput.
- Performs non-parametric hypothesis testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank) and computes 95% empirical bootstrap confidence intervals.
- Generates publication-ready LaTeX tables with clear mean ± std formatting and automated significance markers.
- Creates high-resolution vector figures: multi-curve training dynamics, ablation bar charts, and hyperparameter sensitivity heatmaps.
Deliverables:
- Clean, open-source experimental repository (ablation_benchmark_suite/) with reproducible configuration files.
- Automated pipeline scripts running the full baseline comparison and ablation grid.
- Publication-ready LaTeX tables summarizing baseline comparisons and ablation study results.
- A 4-page experimental evaluation document formatted in standard conference LaTeX style (NeurIPS/ICML format).
modules.mentalModel: A rock-solid empirical section features competitive baselines, equal compute tuning, a thorough ablation study, and statistical significance tests.
modules.tryIt: Execute the complete benchmarking and ablation suite, producing the final comparative table and ablation chart ready for inclusion in a paper.
modules.outcome: You can design, execute, and present empirical machine learning experiments that satisfy the highest standards of top-tier peer review.

levels.title: High-Performance Computing (HPC) & Scaled Research Systems
levels.scope: Transition research codebases from single-GPU workstations to institutional and supercomputing HPC clusters: navigating SLURM batch job schedulers, environment modules, distributed multi-node execution with PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP), DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, and Megatron tensor parallelism; profiling Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU), optimizing NCCL communication collectives, and overcoming out-of-memory (OOM) bottlenecks.
levels.prereqStated: Level 8 (Experimental Design, Ablation Studies & Fair Benchmarking)

modules.name: Supercomputing Infrastructure: SLURM, Environment Modules & Interconnects

objectives.text: - Master institutional and national supercomputing job scheduling using SLURM (Simple Linux Utility for Resource Management).
- Author modular SLURM batch scripts (#SBATCH directives): configuring nodes, tasks-per-node, GPU partitions, time limits, and memory requests.
- Manage large-scale hyperparameter searches and multi-seed sweeps efficiently using SLURM job arrays (--array) with automated output redirection.
- Navigate HPC software module systems (Lmod, Environment Modules): loading compiler toolchains, specific CUDA drivers, and optimized cuDNN libraries.
objectives.group: HPC Software Modules & High-Speed Network Fabrics

objectives.text: - Understand supercomputing network topologies: high-bandwidth InfiniBand (HDR/NDR) fabrics and RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet).
objectives.group: HPC Software Modules & High-Speed Network Fabrics

objectives.text: - Leverage GPUDirect RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) to enable zero-copy GPU-to-GPU data transfers across physical server nodes.
objectives.group: HPC Software Modules & High-Speed Network Fabrics

modules.mentalModel: SLURM is the traffic controller of the supercomputer; precise resource specifications prevent jobs from failing due to memory or time preemption.
modules.tryIt: Write a SLURM batch submission script requesting 2 nodes and 8 GPUs with automated checkpoint recovery and email alerts upon job completion.
modules.outcome: Navigate institutional and laboratory supercomputing environments, submit multi-node batch scripts, and leverage high-speed interconnects.

modules.name: Distributed Data Parallelism: DDP, FSDP & DeepSpeed ZeRO

objectives.text: - Master PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (DDP): multi-process spawning, local rank vs. global rank mapping, and distributed process group initialization.
- Analyze the Ring All-Reduce communication algorithm: synchronizing parameter gradients across N GPUs with 2*(N-1)/N communication volume.
- Implement gradient accumulation to simulate large global batch sizes on hardware with restricted physical VRAM capacity.
- Deconstruct DeepSpeed ZeRO memory sharding: ZeRO-Stage 1 (sharding optimizer states), ZeRO-Stage 2 (gradients), and ZeRO-Stage 3 (model parameters).
- Master PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP): configuring sharding strategies (FULL_SHARD, SHARD_GRAD_OP, NO_SHARD), mixed precision, and backward prefetching.
- Overcome out-of-memory (OOM) errors when scaling model parameters beyond the physical memory capacity of individual GPU cards.

modules.mentalModel: Standard DDP duplicates the entire model on every GPU; FSDP shards model parameters and optimizer states across the cluster, reconstituting them on-the-fly.
modules.tryIt: Convert a standard PyTorch training loop to PyTorch FSDP, training a multi-billion parameter model across multiple GPUs with mixed precision.
modules.outcome: Implement and scale distributed data-parallel training across multi-GPU and multi-node clusters using DDP and FSDP.

modules.name: Model, Pipeline & Tensor Parallelism (Megatron-LM)

objectives.text: - Master intra-layer tensor parallelism (Megatron-LM): splitting linear weight matrices across GPU devices to distribute memory and computation.
- Implement Column Parallel Linear layers (splitting attention QKV projections) and Row Parallel Linear layers (merging projections with all-reduce).
- Maintain communication efficiency: inserting exactly two all-reduce operations per Transformer layer (one in self-attention, one in MLP block).
- Implement inter-layer pipeline parallelism (PP): partitioning sequential Transformer layers across distinct physical GPUs.
- Analyze pipeline bubbles and execution schedules: standard sequential schedules vs. interleaved One-Forward-One-Backward (1F1B) schedules.
- Apply activation checkpointing (gradient checkpointing): trading 30% additional compute to discard intermediate activations and recompute them during backward passes.

modules.mentalModel: Tensor parallelism splits individual layers horizontally across GPUs; pipeline parallelism stacks layers vertically across a chain of GPUs.
modules.tryIt: Implement column-parallel and row-parallel linear layers in PyTorch using distributed communication collectives, verifying numerical equivalence with a monolithic layer.
modules.outcome: Design and execute 3D parallelism (Data + Tensor + Pipeline Parallelism) to train ultra-large models exceeding single-device memory limits.

modules.name: Communication Collectives & Hardware Bottleneck Profiling

objectives.text: - Master fundamental communication primitives in NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library): All-Reduce, Reduce-Scatter, All-Gather, and Broadcast.
- Benchmark inter-GPU communication bandwidth: measuring NVLink intra-node bandwidth (up to 900 GB/s) versus InfiniBand inter-node bandwidth.
- Implement communication-computation overlapping: prefetching next-layer parameters asynchronously while current-layer matrix multiplications execute.
- Profile distributed execution using PyTorch Profiler and NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys): recording kernel timelines and communication overhead.
- Inspect execution traces using Chrome Trace Viewer and TensorBoard: identifying GPU idle bubbles caused by CPU data loading stalls or slow NCCL barriers.
- Diagnose and eliminate straggler nodes: detecting thermal throttling, slow network ports, or uneven batch workloads across distributed workers.

levels.title: Foundation Models, Fine-Tuning & Domain Specialization
levels.scope: Investigate the empirical science of foundation models: empirical scaling laws (Kaplan, Chinchilla), pre-training loss dynamics and stability (spikes, z-loss, weight decay), parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT: LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA), and Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training (DAPT) for specialized sectors such as clinical medicine (BioGPT, Clinical-Camel) and cybersecurity threat intelligence (SecBERT, CyberLLaMA).

modules.name: Empirical Scaling Laws: Kaplan vs Chinchilla Frontiers

objectives.text: - Understand the empirical discovery of scaling laws: test cross-entropy loss scales as a power-law with compute (C), dataset size (D), and parameter count (N).
- Analyze the OpenAI Kaplan et al. formulation: predicting performance gains from small compute budgets to large-scale frontier runs.
- Identify the critical limitation of early scaling regimes: disproportionate allocation of compute toward parameter count while starving token counts.
- Deconstruct the DeepMind Chinchilla scaling law: determining that for optimal compute efficiency, parameters and tokens should scale equally (D ~ 20 * N).
objectives.group: Chinchilla Optimal Compute Frontiers (Hoffmann et al.)

objectives.text: - Fit parametric power-law curves to empirical loss sweeps across small model sizes using non-linear least squares optimization.
objectives.group: Chinchilla Optimal Compute Frontiers (Hoffmann et al.)

objectives.text: - Predict downstream task performance, perplexity thresholds, and phase transitions (e.g., emergence of arithmetic or in-context learning capabilities).
objectives.group: Chinchilla Optimal Compute Frontiers (Hoffmann et al.)

modules.mentalModel: Scaling laws transform AI pre-training from trial-and-error into a predictive engineering science, allowing researchers to predict giant-model loss from small pilot runs.
modules.tryIt: Fit Chinchilla power-law parameters to empirical training runs from 5 small models, and project the optimal parameter-token split for a 10^21 FLOP compute budget.
modules.outcome: Derive and apply empirical scaling laws to predict loss frontiers and compute-optimal resource allocations for pre-training.

modules.name: Pre-Training Dynamics, Loss Stability & Optimization Surgery

objectives.text: - Diagnose catastrophic training loss spikes: uncovering underlying causes including outlier activation vectors, gradient explosions, and FP16 underflow.
- Master numerical stabilization strategies: adopting Bfloat16 (BF16) precision, implementing QK-Norm (normalizing queries and keys before attention), and RMSNorm.
- Apply auxiliary stabilization losses: implementing auxiliary z-loss (penalizing large log-partition functions) to prevent logits from drifting to extreme values.
- Compare learning rate schedules: Cosine Annealing, Linear Warmup-Decay, and modern Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) schedules facilitating continual pre-training.
- Tune decoupled AdamW hyperparameters: analyzing the impact of beta_2 (e.g., 0.95 vs. 0.999), epsilon floor thresholds, and weight decay magnitude.
- Implement gradient norm clipping with adaptive thresholds to suppress anomalous mini-batch gradient shocks without terminating training.

modules.mentalModel: Pre-training stability requires continuous vigilance; small architectural hygiene fixes like QK-Norm and z-loss prevent multi-thousand-dollar training runs from diverging.
modules.tryIt: Simulate an unstable training loop with high learning rates, diagnose the activation outlier pathology, and stabilize the loss trajectory using QK-Norm and z-loss.
modules.outcome: Diagnose and resolve training instabilities, prevent loss spikes, and tune advanced optimization schedules for stable pre-training.

modules.name: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: LoRA, QLoRA & DoRA

objectives.text: - Analyze the intrinsic low dimensionality of parameter updates during task adaptation (Aghajanyan et al.).
- Implement Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) (Hu et al.): freezing pre-trained weights W_0 and decomposing weight updates into low-rank matrices B * A (r << d).
- Tune LoRA hyperparameters: rank r, scaling factor alpha, target modules (attention projections vs. feedforward networks), and dropout.
- Master QLoRA (Dettmers et al.): 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization, Double Quantization, and Paged Optimizers to fine-tune 70B models on consumer GPUs.
- Implement Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) (Liu et al.): decomposing weights into magnitude and directional components to mirror full fine-tuning dynamics.
- Benchmark fine-tuning performance: comparing memory savings, training speed, and validation accuracy against full-parameter fine-tuning baselines.

modules.mentalModel: Fine-tuning does not require modifying all 70 billion parameters; learning low-rank directional update vectors preserves knowledge while adapting to new tasks.
modules.tryIt: Fine-tune a pre-trained open-weight language model on a specialized classification task using QLoRA in 4-bit precision, logging peak VRAM and convergence.
modules.outcome: Implement, optimize, and benchmark parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA) on hardware-constrained research systems.

modules.name: Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training (DAPT) in Specialized Sectors

objectives.text: - Understand Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training (DAPT) (Gururangan et al.): continuing self-supervised pre-training on specialized domain corpora.
- Address catastrophic forgetting: the degradation of general reasoning capabilities when updating weights on specialized single-domain distributions.
- Implement experience replay and corpus mixing: blending 15-20% general pre-training data alongside specialized domain tokens to preserve core linguistic and logical abilities.
- Analyze tokenization pathologies in specialized domains: how standard tokenizers excessively fragment medical terminology or cybersecurity hex code.
- Train custom domain tokenizers (Byte-Pair Encoding BPE) on medical literature (PubMed) or cybersecurity reports (CVEs, threat intelligence).
- Expand model vocabularies with new domain tokens, initializing new embedding weights using mean projections of constituent subwords.

modules.mentalModel: DAPT teaches a generalist model the specialized vocabulary, syntax, and relational knowledge of a scientific domain without erasing its foundational intellect.
modules.tryIt: Perform Continual Pre-Training of a small language model on a curated corpus of clinical abstracts, tracking both clinical perplexity and general reasoning benchmarks.
modules.outcome: Execute Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training for specialized sectors while mitigating catastrophic forgetting through corpus blending.

- Implement completion-only loss masking: calculating cross-entropy loss exclusively on assistant response tokens while masking prompt and instruction tokens.
- Elicit structured Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning: training models to articulate step-by-step intermediate rationales before outputting clinical or security conclusions.
- Filter synthetic instruction datasets for contamination, factual hallucination, and stylistic repetition using automated rule-based and model-based heuristics.

levels.title: Explainability, Interpretability & Trustworthy AI
levels.scope: Unpack the internal mechanisms of black-box models to satisfy scientific peer review and regulatory standards (FDA clinical AI clearance, EU AI Act): feature attribution (SHAP, Integrated Gradients, Grad-CAM for medical scans), mechanistic interpretability (linear representation probing, activation patching, attention head visualization), sparse autoencoders (SAEs) for monosemantic feature discovery, and counterfactual explanation generation for clinical diagnostic and cybersecurity triage decisions.

modules.name: Feature Attribution: SHAP, Integrated Gradients & Saliency

objectives.text: - Master the axiomatic foundations of Shapley values: efficiency, symmetry, dummy player, and additivity in cooperative game theory.
- Implement KernelSHAP for black-box models and TreeSHAP (Lundberg et al.) for high-speed exact attribution in gradient boosted trees.
- Apply SHAP to clinical tabular models (identifying patient risk factors for sepsis) and cybersecurity intrusion classifiers (pinpointing anomalous packet flags).
- Analyze the failure of vanilla gradient saliency maps: gradient saturation, threshold sensitivity, and lack of implementation invariance.
- Implement Integrated Gradients (Sundararajan et al.): accumulating path integrals from a neutral baseline to the input to satisfy Completeness and Implementation Invariance.
- Apply Grad-CAM and Grad-CAM++ to convolutional and vision Transformer architectures, visualizing spatial attention maps on clinical radiographs.

modules.mentalModel: Integrated Gradients traces a straight-line interpolation between a neutral baseline and the input, measuring how every feature contributes to the final logit.
modules.tryIt: Compute Integrated Gradients on a medical image classifier in PyTorch, verify that attributions sum to the difference between output and baseline logits, and plot the heatmap.

modules.name: Linear Representation Probing & Latent Geometry

objectives.text: - Understand representation probing: training simple linear classifiers on intermediate hidden activations to test whether specific concepts are linearly represented.
- Probe deep neural networks for medical concepts (e.g., patient age, smoker status) or cybersecurity concepts (e.g., protocol types, attack family) across sequential layers.
- Map the trajectory of concept emergence: demonstrating how low-level superficial features peak in early layers while high-level semantic concepts form in late layers.
- Avoid the "probing trap": distinguishing whether a probe is discovering a representation learned by the model or merely memorizing the task itself.
- Implement Control Tasks (Hewitt & Liang): evaluating linear probes against randomized control labels to measure probe selectivity.
- Analyze representation geometry: computing representation similarity matrices (Centered Kernel Alignment CKA) to compare latent spaces across model checkpoints.

modules.mentalModel: A linear probe is a scientific stethoscope listening to hidden activations; if a concept cannot be extracted linearly, the model has not explicitly disentangled it.
modules.tryIt: Extract hidden states across all layers of a pre-trained Transformer on clinical notes, train linear probes for mortality prediction, and plot probe accuracy across depth.
modules.outcome: Execute rigorous linear probing experiments, evaluate concept emergence across layer depth, and validate probe selectivity using control tasks.

modules.name: Mechanistic Interpretability: Activation Patching & Circuits

objectives.text: - Master the paradigm of mechanistic interpretability: reverse-engineering neural networks into understandable computational algorithms and functional circuits.
- Implement activation patching (causal mediation analysis): swapping intermediate activations between clean and corrupted inputs to isolate causal components.
- Locate factual knowledge and reasoning circuits in Transformers: identifying specific MLP layers or attention heads responsible for specific predictions.
- Analyze attention head specialization: identifying Induction Heads (responsible for in-context pattern copying), Duplicate Token Heads, and Inhibition Heads.
- Map end-to-end computational subgraphs (circuits) within models performing specific domain logic (e.g., matching clinical symptoms to prescription decisions).
- Test circuit completeness: verifying that pruning all neurons and attention heads outside the discovered circuit preserves task performance.

modules.mentalModel: Mechanistic interpretability treats neural networks like biological brains, using targeted activation lesions to identify causal cognitive circuits.
modules.tryIt: Perform activation patching on a small Transformer model solving an algorithmic task, isolating the exact attention heads that perform in-context copying.
modules.outcome: Trace causal computational circuits in neural networks using activation patching and identify specialized attention head mechanisms.

modules.name: Dictionary Learning & Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs)

objectives.text: - Understand polysemanticity: individual neurons activate for multiple completely unrelated concepts due to superposition (compressing more concepts than dimensions).
objectives.group: The Polysemanticity Crisis in Neural Representations

objectives.text: - Formalize the superposition hypothesis: neural networks utilize non-orthogonal almost-independent direction vectors in high-dimensional vector spaces.
objectives.group: The Polysemanticity Crisis in Neural Representations

objectives.text: - Contrast polysemantic biological neurons with the goal of isolating pure, monosemantic research features.
objectives.group: The Polysemanticity Crisis in Neural Representations

objectives.text: - Architect an overcomplete Sparse Autoencoder (SAE): expanding intermediate hidden states into a higher-dimensional dictionary (e.g., 8x to 32x hidden dimension).
- Enforce strict sparsity: training SAEs with L1 regularization penalties or modern TopK activation functions to ensure only a handful of dictionary features fire per token.
- Uncover interpretable monosemantic features: discovering individual dictionary latent directions corresponding to clinical disease concepts or malicious shellcode strings.

modules.mentalModel: Sparse autoencoders untangle the entangled web of polysemantic neurons into an expanded dictionary of clean, interpretable monosemantic concepts.

modules.name: Counterfactual Explanations & Algorithmic Recourse

objectives.text: - Formulate counterfactual explanations from first principles: finding the smallest perturbation delta applied to input X such that the model prediction flips from class Y to Y*.
- Balance competing objectives: minimizing input distance (L1/L2 norm), maximizing target class probability, and enforcing domain plausibility constraints.
- Prevent invalid recourse: ensuring immutable features (e.g., patient biological age, system hardware UUIDs) cannot be modified in counterfactual recommendations.
- Enforce manifold constraints: ensuring counterfactual clinical patient states remain on the valid physiological manifold (e.g., blood pressure cannot be zero while alive).
- Generate counterfactual cyber incident explanations: demonstrating the minimum packet modifications required to transform an intrusion alert into benign traffic.
- Present recourse recommendations: providing actionable, human-interpretable guidance for physicians evaluating automated diagnostic alerts or security analysts triaging alarms.

modules.mentalModel: A counterfactual answer does not just explain why a model made a decision; it shows what must change in the real world to alter the outcome.
modules.tryIt: Implement a counterfactual optimization algorithm using gradient descent on a clinical tabular classifier, finding the minimal actionable lifestyle change to reduce cardiac risk.
modules.outcome: Formulate and optimize plausible counterfactual explanations with domain-specific feasibility constraints for healthcare and cybersecurity applications.

levels.title: AI Alignment, Robustness & Adversarial Defense
levels.scope: Conduct rigorous research into adversarial robustness and alignment: generating white-box and black-box adversarial attacks (FGSM, PGD, Carlini-Wagner) on medical image classification and cybersecurity intrusion detection systems (evasion attacks on malware classifiers); adversarial training and certified defense bounds; preference alignment methodologies (RLHF, DPO, KTO); auditing demographic bias and algorithmic fairness across diverse patient populations.

modules.name: Adversarial Attacks: White-Box, Black-Box & Evasion Vectors

objectives.text: - Formulate the adversarial perturbation optimization problem: maximizing loss subject to an L_p norm constraint (L_infinity, L_2) on perturbation delta.
- Derive the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) (Goodfellow et al.) as a one-step linearization of the adversarial loss landscape.
- Implement Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) (Madry et al.) as the standard multi-step first-order white-box adversary with random restarts.
- Formulate the Carlini-Wagner (C&W) optimization attack: finding minimal L_2 distortion while bypassing gradient masking and defensive distillation.
- Execute black-box adversarial attacks: leveraging transferability across substitute surrogate models and gradient-free zeroth-order optimization (NES).
- Demonstrate extreme vulnerability in medical imaging: adding imperceptible high-frequency pixel noise to chest X-rays that flips diagnostic outputs with 99% confidence.

modules.mentalModel: Deep neural networks have linear behavior in high-dimensional spaces; tiny aligned perturbations across thousands of dimensions accumulate into massive logit swings.
modules.tryIt: Implement a PGD L_infinity attack in PyTorch against a pre-trained radiological classifier, plot the perturbation noise image, and record the accuracy drop.
modules.outcome: Implement first-order and optimization-based adversarial attacks to evaluate the adversarial vulnerability of deep learning models.

modules.name: Adversarial Training, Robust Optimization & Certified Bounds

objectives.text: - Formalize adversarial training as a robust min-max game (Madry et al.): minimizing expected risk under worst-case inner-maximization adversarial perturbations.
- Implement PGD adversarial training: dynamically generating adversarial examples during every training mini-batch and optimizing model weights on corrupted inputs.
- Analyze the fundamental trade-off between standard accuracy and adversarial robustness (Zhang et al. TRADES formulation).
- Understand why empirical defenses frequently succumb to stronger adaptive attacks (gradient obfuscation, shattered gradients).
- Master certified robustness: providing mathematical guarantees that no perturbation within an L_2 radius R can flip the model prediction.
- Implement Randomized Smoothing (Cohen et al.): certifying robust classifications by convolving base classifiers with isotropic Gaussian noise.

modules.mentalModel: Empirical defenses patch specific attack tools; certified robustness provides a mathematical guarantee of safety within a defined perturbation sphere.
modules.tryIt: Train a model using PGD adversarial training in PyTorch, evaluate robust accuracy against increasing perturbation epsilon, and compute certified radii via randomized smoothing.
modules.outcome: Formulate robust optimization objectives, implement adversarial training, and compute mathematically certified robustness bounds.

modules.name: Cybersecurity Evasion & Malware Feature Manipulation

objectives.text: - Differentiate between feature-space attacks (perturbing feature vectors directly) and problem-space attacks (modifying actual executable binary files).

objectives.text: - Account for inverse mapping and domain preservation constraints: ensuring modified malicious binaries execute correctly and preserve exploit functionality.
objectives.group: Feature-Space vs. Problem-Space Attacks in Security

objectives.text: - Implement structural evasion: injecting benign byte sequences into Portable Executable (PE) slack spaces and appending benign overlay sections.
objectives.group: Feature-Space vs. Problem-Space Attacks in Security

objectives.text: - Evade gradient boosted decision trees (Ember benchmark) and neural network detectors by crafting functional malware variants using genetic algorithms and RL agents.
objectives.group: Evading Machine Learning Intrusion & Malware Detectors

objectives.group: Evading Machine Learning Intrusion & Malware Detectors

objectives.text: - Implement robust malware feature extractors that resist structural manipulation and strip non-semantic byte artifacts prior to classification.
objectives.group: Evading Machine Learning Intrusion & Malware Detectors

modules.name: Preference Alignment: RLHF, DPO & Kahneman-Tversky Optimization

objectives.text: - Master the canonical three-stage RLHF pipeline: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reward modeling on pairwise preferences, and PPO policy optimization.
- Derive the Bradley-Terry preference model: estimating the latent reward function r(x, y) from pairwise human comparison datasets.
- Prevent policy collapse and reward hacking: enforcing a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence penalty between the fine-tuned policy and the reference model.
- Deconstruct Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) (Rafailov et al.): analytically reparameterizing the reward function in terms of the policy itself.
- Derive the closed-form DPO objective, eliminating the need to train a separate reward model or run unstable reinforcement learning loops during training.
- Explore Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO): aligning models using binary feedback (thumbs up / thumbs down) based on prospect theory loss functions.

modules.mentalModel: DPO proves that the optimal policy implicitly defines its own reward function, allowing direct preference alignment via standard cross-entropy loss.
modules.tryIt: Implement the DPO loss function in PyTorch from scratch, train a small language model on a pairwise preference dataset, and track implicit reward margins.
modules.outcome: Formulate and implement preference alignment objectives (RLHF, DPO, KTO) to align foundation models with human values and domain criteria.

modules.name: Algorithmic Fairness, Demographic Disparity & Bias Auditing

objectives.text: - Formalize disparate impact and demographic fairness criteria: Demographic Parity (P(Y_hat = 1 | A = 0) = P(Y_hat = 1 | A = 1)) across protected attributes A.
- Formulate Equalized Odds and Equality of Opportunity (Hardt et al.): conditioning false positive and true positive rates to be equal across demographic subgroups.
- Understand the impossibility theorem of algorithmic fairness (Kleinberg et al.): proving that calibration and equalized odds cannot hold simultaneously unless base rates are identical.
- Audit clinical models (MIMIC-IV / CheXpert) for performance disparities across demographic subgroups (e.g., race, biological sex, age, socioeconomic insurance status).
- Identify underdiagnosis bias: models exhibiting significantly higher false negative rates in marginalized patient populations despite high aggregate accuracy.

modules.name: Contrastive Vision-Language Learning: CLIP & BioMedCLIP

objectives.text: - Derive the symmetric cross-entropy contrastive loss over paired visual and textual batches (Radford et al. CLIP).
- Analyze learned temperature parameters and the catastrophic memory scaling of global softmax normalization across massive distributed batch sizes.

- Train specialized contrastive models on domain-specific scientific image-text pairs (e.g., BioMedCLIP trained on PubMed Central figures and captions).
- Formulate zero-shot domain classification: generating clinical prompt templates (e.g., "a chest radiograph showing signs of [CLASS]") for pathology identification.

- Master two-stage multimodal training: Stage 1 visual-language alignment (training the projection layer while freezing backbones) and Stage 2 end-to-end instruction tuning.

modules.name: Flagship Project 1: Medical Image Segmentation & Volumetric Biomarker Discovery

objectives.text: - Select a competitive 3D volumetric medical imaging benchmark from the Medical Segmentation Decathlon or BraTS (Brain Tumor Segmentation).

modules.outcome: A scientifically verified 3D medical image segmentation research codebase and clinical biomarker evaluation report meeting peer-reviewed medical imaging standards.

modules.name: Flagship Project 2: Cybersecurity Threat Graph Intrusion Detection & Botnet Investigation

objectives.text: - Transform raw network flow captures (CIC-IDS-2017) and enterprise host provenance logs into large-scale, directed heterogeneous property graphs using PyTorch Geometric.
- Architect an inductive Graph Neural Network (GAT with edge features or Temporal Graph Network) capable of modeling dynamic enterprise network topologies.

- Profile runtime computational efficiency on an HPC GPU cluster: measuring memory scaling, node sampling throughput, and real-time inference latency.

modules.outcome: A novel graph-based cybersecurity threat detection framework that identifies coordinated attack campaigns across complex enterprise network topologies.

- Evaluate a comprehensive suite of open-weight (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) and proprietary foundation models under standardized zero-shot and few-shot Chain-of-Thought conditions.

modules.name: Flagship Project 4: Mechanistic Circuit Discovery in Clinical Decision Networks

objectives.text: - Select a critical clinical reasoning capability in an open-weight foundation model (e.g., differential diagnosis, contraindication detection, or dosage calculation).

- Extract contrastive activation steering vectors and demonstrate targeted behavioral steering during generation without increasing general language perplexity.
- Author an interactive research report featuring causal circuit wiring diagrams, activation heatmaps, and mechanistic ablation proofs.

modules.outcome: An end-to-end mechanistic interpretability discovery identifying the internal computational circuit and demonstrating precise latent steering in clinical AI.
